title: The Alibi of Greywater Bay
premise: Theo Ashgrove, a night-shift taxi dispatcher in the fog-bound town of Greywater Bay, receives a letter confessing to the drowning of local judge Edmund Vail — postmarked one day after the judge's funeral. The letter claims the real killer is still free and names a witness, Marisol Quade, whom the whole town believes died three years ago. As Theo follows the confession's clues through dispatch logs, old fares, and the town's buried loyalties, he discovers his own late father was entangled in the night of Vail's death. In the end Theo finds Marisol alive and hidden in a decommissioned lighthouse, exposes the killer — Vail's protégé, prosecutor Dana Whitlock — and must choose between protecting the confession's author, his first love, and telling a truth that will shatter the town.
about_author: Sebastian Nystrom is the pen name of a former harbor-town journalist who spent a decade covering small-court crime before turning to fiction. He writes at night, claiming the dark hours keep the secrets honest.

chapters.title: The Last Fare
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. On a rain-slicked night shift, Theo dispatches cabs around Greywater Bay and takes one last call from Judge Edmund Vail hours before the judge is found drowned. The chapter establishes Theo's insomnia, his grief for his dead father, and the town's habit of keeping quiet. Emotional beat: dread disguised as routine.

chapters.title: Postmarked After
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A week after the funeral, an unsigned confession letter arrives, postmarked the day after Vail's burial. It admits to being present at the drowning, insists the writer is not the killer, and names Marisol Quade — a witness officially dead for three years. Theo's hands shake; he recognizes the handwriting's looped 'g' from somewhere in his past. Beat: the ordinary life cracks open.

chapters.title: A Town That Drowns Quietly
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo walks the funeral's aftermath: the harbor, the diner, the courthouse steps. Everyone performs grief, but small details don't fit — the judge's car moved, his coat dry. Theo learns the trial of dockworker Sam Okafor, accused of Vail's murder, begins in five weeks. Beat: the town's loyalty is a wall, not a comfort.

chapters.title: The Loop in the G
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Comparing the confession to old letters from his first love, Lena Vail — the judge's estranged daughter — Theo suspects she wrote it. He tracks her to a rented room above the chandlery. Their reunion is charged with old love and older blame. She neither confirms nor denies. Beat: love as both suspect and shelter.

chapters.title: Dispatch Records, 2:14 A.M.
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Pulling the company's night logs, Theo finds a cab dispatched to Vail's street at 2:14 a.m. — logged by his own father, years ago, in a nearly identical case: the 'accidental' drowning of Marisol Quade. Two deaths, one pattern. Beat: the past stops being past.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Drowned
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV, in flashback. Three years earlier: Marisol, a courthouse clerk, saw something she shouldn't have in Judge Vail's chambers and fled; her 'drowning' was arranged. The chapter reveals she trusted one person with the truth — and that person's identity is withheld. Beat: fear sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: Coffee with the Prosecutor
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Dana Whitlock, Vail's protégé and the trial's prosecutor, invites Theo for coffee — too warm, too curious. She knows about the letter. She offers to 'protect' Theo if he hands it over. Theo lies for the first time in his life. Beat: charm with teeth.

chapters.title: Lena's Version
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena admits she found her father's private files after his death — records of payments to keep Marisol quiet — and wrote the confession to force the town to look. But she swears she didn't send it, and didn't know about the 2:14 a.m. cab. Someone else is moving the pieces. Beat: love against duty, both bleeding.

chapters.title: The Chandlery Burn
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The chandlery above Lena's room catches fire; the confession's draft pages are destroyed. Theo drags Lena out through smoke. In the ashes he finds a melted key tag from the old lighthouse keeper's cottage. Beat: the enemy escalates; Theo stops being an observer.

chapters.title: Sam Okafor's Silence
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. In county holding, Sam Okafor tells Theo he saw a car with government plates at the dock that night — and that his lawyer told him to plead out. The lawyer's retainer traces back to Whitlock's office. Beat: the machinery of the trial is rigged, and Theo sees the gears.

chapters.title: What My Father Logged
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. In his father's locked dispatch box, Theo finds the old route card for the 2:14 a.m. call — the pickup address is the lighthouse keeper's cottage. His father didn't just log the fare; he was the driver. Beat: grief curdles into complicity.

chapters.title: Halfway Rock
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo hikes to the decommissioned lighthouse at Halfway Rock through fog. The cottage is lived in: fresh bread, a radio tuned to the taxi band. He hears footsteps and is struck from behind. Beat: hope ambushed by violence.

chapters.title: The Woman at the Light
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol has been keeping Theo captive-gentle, deciding whether he's a threat — since she was the one who struck him. She reveals she sent the confession, not Lena, using handwriting she knew would point to Lena to draw out the killer. Beat: the confession was bait, and Theo took the hook.

chapters.title: The Night of Two Drownings
chapters.summary: Marisol and Theo's POV alternating. Marisol tells the whole truth: three years ago she saw Whitlock take a bribe from the harbor syndicate in Vail's chambers; Vail covered it, then grew a conscience and was going to recuse himself from the syndicate's cases. Marisol's drowning was staged by Vail himself to save her. Beat: the judge was both coward and protector.

chapters.title: The Fare at 2:14
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo finally decodes his father's role: the judge hired his father's cab that night three years ago to move Marisol to the lighthouse — and on the night of his own death, Vail called the same dispatcher to send a message to Marisol: he was ready to testify. The message never arrived; Whitlock intercepted the call. Beat: his father's loyalty was love, not betrayal.

chapters.title: Trial Week
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Jury selection begins; Whitlock's case against Sam Okafor is airtight and false. Theo, Lena, and Marisol plan to surface Marisol's testimony, but Whitlock announces a surprise witness of her own — a taxi dispatcher who will place Okafor at the dock. The dispatcher is Theo's replacement at the company. Beat: the noose closes on an innocent man.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Whitlock's POV. Whitlock confronts Theo privately: she knows Marisol lives, knows about the lighthouse, and offers Theo the thing he wants most — his father's name cleared, sealed records, no charges — if Marisol stays dead. Theo walks out without answering, and we see Whitlock order a tail on Lena. Beat: duty and love pull in opposite directions, and the villain shows her logic.

chapters.title: Fog Signal
chapters.summary: Theo and Marisol's POV. Whitlock's men raid Halfway Rock; Marisol escapes through the fog using the lighthouse's old fog signal as a decoy, while Theo leads the raiders astray in a taxi with the meter running. They regroup with Lena at the harbor master's office, where Theo's father's old logs are archived — the last physical proof. Beat: fugitive love, working as a team at last.

chapters.title: The Archived Night
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. In the archive they find the dispatch tape from Vail's last night: the judge's own voice, booking a fare to the courthouse to deliver his recusal letter, and Whitlock's voice on the office line arranging the dock meeting. The tape also clears Okafor — his cab fare home is logged at the time of death. Beat: the truth, finally physical and undeniable.

chapters.title: The Stand
chapters.summary: Theo, Marisol, and Lena's POV. Mid-trial, Marisol walks into the courtroom alive. Whitlock's cross-examination turns vicious, but Theo takes the stand as the dispatcher who traced the 2:14 call, and the tape is played. Whitlock unravels on the record, tries to recast herself as a witness, and is arrested as the gallery watches. Beat: climax — truth wins, loudly, in the room built to bury it.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Owes
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. In the aftermath, the town must digest what its silence protected. Theo visits his father's grave and reads the old route card aloud, forgiving them both. Lena chooses to leave Greywater Bay to rebuild her father's name from outside; she asks Theo to come. Beat: love and duty reconciled, not resolved.

chapters.title: Night Shift, Clear Sky
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, epilogue. Months later, Theo takes one last night shift before deciding his future. A fare asks him, as Vail once did, whether the fog ever lifts. Theo answers that it does — you just have to drive through it. He locks the dispatch office, leaves the confession letter in the archive, and walks toward the bus that will take him to Lena. Beat: quiet resolution, open road.
